methodology: Both the original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved breaking down complex sentences into simpler, more manageable statements. For the original research topic, the decomposition focused on the functional requirements, the Rule 110 definition, the system architecture (512 cells), and the boundary conditions. For the generated technical specification, the decomposition focused on the combinational logic function, the Boolean expression, the truth table representation, the boundary conditions, and the parallel computation aspect. The timing logic summary was also considered, focusing on sequential circuit type, timing dependencies, and implementation details.
mindtraced_atomic_units: The system consists of a one-dimensional array of 512 cells (q[511:0])
Each cell can be either on (1) or off (0)
The state of the entire system advances by one time step on each clock cycle
The next state of each cell q[i] depends on its current state and the states of its two neighbors, q[i-1] and q[i+1], according to the Rule 110 table
Boundary cells q[0] and q[511] should consider their non-existent neighbors q[-1] and q[512] to be off (0)
A synchronous active-high load input allows initializing the state of the system
When the load input is asserted, the state of the system is loaded with the data provided on the data[511:0] input
spec_atomic_units: The combinational logic calculates the next state of each cell in the 512-cell system based on Rule 110
For each cell `i` (where `0 <= i <= 511`), the next state `next_q[i]` is determined by the current states of its left neighbor `left`, itself `center`, and its right neighbor `right`
Boundary conditions: `left` is 0 when `i` is 0, and `right` is 0 when `i` is 511
Rule 110 logic can be expressed as the Boolean expression: `next_q[i] = (left & center & ~right) | (left & ~center & right) | (~left & center & right) | (~left & ~center & right)`
Combinational logic operates independently for each cell, allowing for parallel computation of the next state of all 512 cells
The system consists of 512 cells, each capable of being in one of two states (0 or 1)
The cells at the boundaries of the system (q[-1] and q[512]) are defined as zero (off)
If `i == 0`, then `left = 0`. If `i == 511`, then `right = 0`. Otherwise, `left = q[i - 1]` and `right = q[i + 1]`
The output of the combinational logic is a 512-bit signal `next_q[511:0]`
The module implements a 512-cell Rule 110 cellular automaton
The output `q` changes only on the rising edge of `clk`
When `load` is high, `q` is loaded with `data` on the rising edge of `clk`
When `load` is low, `q` is updated with the next state of the cellular automaton, calculated based on the current state of `q` and Rule 110, also on the rising edge of `clk`
